questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा क्षेत्र 1866 में एकीकृत इटली का हिस्सा बना ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following regions became a part of unified Italy in 1866?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Venetia. Venetia was incorporated into unified Italy in 1866 following the Austro-Prussian War, in which Austria was defeated and ceded Venetia to Italy through French mediation. Sardinia-Piedmont was the original base of Italian unification and was not 'added' in 1866. Sicily was unified much earlier under Garibaldi in 1860. The Papal States were only annexed in 1870.
questions.chapter: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe

questions.text:
उन्नीसवीं सदी तक लोगों के यूरोप से अमेरिका जाने के निम्नलिखित कारणों को पढ़िए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
I. गरीबी और भूख
II. गुलामों की खरीद-फरोख्त
III. बीमारियों का बोलबाला
IV. धार्मिक टकराव और दंड
questions.text_english:
Read the following reasons of migration of people from Europe to America till the 19th century and choose the correct option:
I. Poverty and hunger
II. Slaves for sale
III. Wide spread of diseases
IV. Religious conflicts and persecution

options.A: केवल I, II और III सही हैं।
options.B: केवल II, III और IV सही हैं।
options.C: केवल I, III और IV सही हैं।
options.D: केवल I, II और IV सही हैं।

options_english.A: Only I, II and III are correct.
options_english.B: Only II, III and IV are correct.
options_english.C: Only I, III and IV are correct.
options_english.D: Only I, II and IV are correct.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Only I, III and IV are correct. People migrated from Europe to America due to poverty and hunger, widespread diseases that drove them to seek better living conditions, and religious conflicts and persecution. The slave trade (Option II) refers to the forced movement of Africans to the Americas and was not a reason for European migration. Hence, I, III, and IV are the correct reasons.
questions.chapter: The Making of a Global World

questions.text: 'बुक ऑफ मार्वेल्स' के लेखक हैं :
questions.text_english: The author of 'Book of Marvels' is:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Marco Polo. 'Book of Marvels' (also known as 'The Travels of Marco Polo') was written by Marco Polo, the Venetian explorer who traveled to China and Asia in the 13th century. Columbus, Vasco da Gama, and Alfred Crosby are renowned explorers and historians but are not associated with this particular book.
questions.chapter: The Making of a Global World

questions.text: मान लीजिए कि आप 15वीं शताब्दी की प्रिंट संस्कृति पर शोध कर रहे हैं। निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा आपके शोध का सबसे महत्वपूर्ण लाभ होगा ?
questions.text_english: Assume you are doing research on 15th century print culture. Which of the following would be the most significant advantage for your research?

options.C: पाठों को हाथ से कॉपी करने की क्षमता में बढ़ोतरी
options.D: प्रिंट में तेज़ी और सटीकता में वृद्धि

options_english.C: Increase in the ability to copy text by hand
options_english.D: Increased speed and accuracy of print

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Increased speed and accuracy of print. The 15th century witnessed Gutenberg's printing press, which revolutionized print culture by enabling the rapid and accurate reproduction of texts. This is the defining characteristic of 15th century print culture. Options A and B are indirect benefits and not the core advantage. Option C refers to manual copying, which was the pre-print era practice, not a benefit of print culture.
questions.chapter: Print Culture and the Modern World

questions.text:
भारत में वनों के निम्नलिखित वर्गों को क्षेत्रफल की दृष्टि से सबसे अधिक से सबसे कम के क्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
I. आरक्षित
II. रक्षित
III. अवर्गीकृत
questions.text_english:
Arrange the following categories of forests in India from the largest to the smallest in terms of area and choose the correct option:
I. Reserved
II. Protected
III. Unclassed
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) I, II, III. In India, Reserved Forests cover the largest area (about 54% of total forest area), followed by Protected Forests (about 29%), and Unclassed Forests cover the smallest proportion (about 17%). Reserved forests are under the strictest government control, which contributes to their larger area designation.

questions.text: 'सरिस्का बाघ रिज़र्व' निम्नलिखित में से किस राज्य में स्थित है ?
questions.text_english: 'Sariska Tiger Reserve' is located in which one of the following states?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Rajasthan. Sariska Tiger Reserve is located in the Alwar district of Rajasthan. It is one of India's significant tiger reserves managed under Project Tiger. Madhya Pradesh is home to Kanha and Bandhavgarh reserves, Maharashtra hosts Tadoba, and Uttar Pradesh has Dudhwa Tiger Reserve.

questions.text:
स्तंभ I का स्तंभ II से मिलान कीजिए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
स्तंभ I (बाँध) — स्तंभ II (नदी)
a. हीराकुड — i. चम्बल
b. गाँधी सागर — ii. कृष्णा
c. नागार्जुन सागर — iii. कावेरी
d. मेटूर — iv. महानदी
questions.text_english:
Match Column I with Column II and choose the correct option:
Column I (Dam) — Column II (River)
a. Hirakud — i. Chambal
b. Gandhi Sagar — ii. Krishna
c. Nagarjuna Sagar — iii. Kaveri
d. Mettur — iv. Mahanadi
questions.instruction_line: स्तंभ I का स्तंभ II से मिलान कीजिए
questions.instruction_line_english: Match Column I with Column II
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii. Hirakud Dam is built on the Mahanadi River (iv), Gandhi Sagar Dam is on the Chambal River (i), Nagarjuna Sagar Dam is on the Krishna River (ii), and Mettur Dam is on the Kaveri River (iii). This correct matching reflects the major multipurpose river valley projects of India.
questions.topic: Major dams and rivers of India

questions.text: कृष्णा – गोदावरी मुद्दे में शामिल प्रमुख राज्यों से संबंधित सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
questions.text_english: Choose the correct option regarding major states involved in the Krishna-Godavari issue:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Maharashtra, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh. The Krishna-Godavari river water dispute primarily involves Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Andhra Pradesh, as these states share the catchment areas and river basins of both the Krishna and Godavari rivers. The dispute relates to the allocation of river waters among these states for irrigation and drinking water purposes.

questions.text: कल्पना कीजिए कि आप जनवरी में दिल्ली से चंडीगढ़ एक शादी में शामिल होने के लिए, सड़क मार्ग से जा रहे हैं। यात्रा के दौरान आप निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी फसल खेतों में प्रमुखता से देखेंगे ?
questions.text_english: Imagine you are travelling from Delhi to Chandigarh to attend a wedding, by road in January. Which of the following crops will you notice prominently in the fields during the journey?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Wheat. January falls in the Rabi (winter) cropping season. The Delhi-Chandigarh route passes through Punjab and Haryana, which are the major wheat-growing states. Wheat is sown in November-December and harvested in March-April, so in January the wheat fields would be prominently visible. Paddy and Maize are Kharif crops grown in summer, and Jowar is also a Kharif crop.
questions.topic: Cropping seasons in India — Rabi crops

questions.text:
नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं। ये अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) हैं। दोनों कथनों को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़िए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
अभिकथन (A) : खनिज हमारे जीवन के अति अनिवार्य भाग हैं।
कारण (R) : सभी सजीव वस्तुओं को खनिजों की आवश्यकता होती है।
questions.text_english:
Two statements are given below. They are Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Read both the statements carefully and choose the correct option:
Assertion (A): Minerals are an indispensable part of our lives.
Reason (R): All living things need minerals.

options.A: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं और (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या है।
options.B: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।

options_english.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options_english.B: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). Both the Assertion and Reason are true, but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion. Minerals are indeed indispensable to our lives because they are used in industries, construction, technology, and everyday products — not merely because living things need them biologically. The Reason (R) is a biological fact but does not explain why minerals are economically and technologically indispensable in human life.

questions.text:
स्तंभ I का स्तंभ II से मिलान कीजिए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
स्तंभ I (खनिज) — स्तंभ II (प्रमुख खानें)
a. लौह अयस्क — i. गया
b. अभ्रक — ii. सिंगरौली
c. बॉक्साइट — iii. चंद्रपुर
d. कोयला — iv. मैकाल
questions.text_english:
Match Column I with Column II and choose the correct option:
Column I (Minerals) — Column II (Major Mines)
a. Iron ore — i. Gaya
b. Mica — ii. Singarauli
c. Bauxite — iii. Chandrapur
d. Coal — iv. Maikala
questions.instruction_line: स्तंभ I का स्तंभ II से मिलान कीजिए
questions.instruction_line_english: Match Column I with Column II
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii. Iron ore has major mines in Chandrapur (iii), Mica is found around Gaya in Bihar (i), Bauxite deposits are found in the Maikala range (iv), and Coal is mined at Singarauli (ii), which is one of India's largest coal fields located in Madhya Pradesh. This matching reflects the major mineral-producing regions of India.
questions.topic: Major mineral producing areas of India

questions.text: बेल्जियम ने अपनी बहुसंख्यकवाद की समस्या का समाधान निम्नलिखित में से किस प्रकार की शासन व्यवस्था को सुदृढ़ करके किया ?
questions.text_english: Belgium solved its problem of majoritarianism by strengthening which of the following types of government?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Federal. Belgium, having a diverse linguistic community of Dutch-speaking Flemish and French-speaking Walloons, adopted a federal form of government. Power was divided between the central government and regional governments. This arrangement ensured that no single linguistic community could dominate the others, thus resolving the problem of majoritarianism through power-sharing.

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित में से सही सुमेलित युग्म का चयन कीजिए :
(देश) — (व्यवस्था)
questions.text_english:
Choose the correctly matched pair from the following:
(Country) — (System)
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Spain — Federal. Spain has a federal-type system where significant autonomy is granted to its regions (like Catalonia, Basque Country). Canada and Australia are also federal countries, not unitary, making options A and C incorrect. Bolivia has a unitary system. Hence, Spain–Federal is the correctly matched pair.
questions.topic: Types of government — Federal vs Unitary

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन-से राजनीतिक दल के मुख्य घटक हैं ? सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
I. नेता
II. सक्रिय सदस्य
III. समर्थक
IV. दबाव समूह
questions.text_english:
Which of the following are the main components of a political party? Choose the correct option:
I. Leaders
II. Active members
III. Followers
IV. Pressure groups

options.A: केवल I, II और III सही हैं।
options.B: केवल II, III और IV सही हैं।
options.C: केवल I, III और IV सही हैं।
options.D: केवल I, II और IV सही हैं।

options_english.A: Only I, II and III are correct.
options_english.B: Only II, III and IV are correct.
options_english.C: Only I, III and IV are correct.
options_english.D: Only I, II and IV are correct.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Only I, II and III are correct. The three main components of a political party are Leaders (who take decisions and guide the party), Active members (who participate in party activities), and Followers or supporters (who vote for and support the party). Pressure groups (IV) are separate organisations that influence political parties but are not components of a political party themselves.

questions.text:
'विश्व मानव विकास सूचकांक' से संबंधित निम्नलिखित तालिका का अध्ययन कीजिए और उसके नीचे दिए गए प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए :
दिए गए देशों में से, निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा देश 'मानव विकास सूचकांक' में उच्चतम स्थान रखता है ?
questions.text_english:
Study the following table related to 'World Human Development Index' and answer the question given below:
Amongst the given countries, which one of the following countries has the highest rank in 'Human Development Index'?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) India. In the given table, a lower rank number indicates a higher position in the Human Development Index. India has rank 130, which is the lowest numerical rank among the four countries listed, meaning India has the highest HDI among Pakistan (150), Nepal (149), and Myanmar (148).

questions.text: 'X' एक कस्बे में रहता है। वह फूलों की खेती के साथ-साथ पशुपालन भी करता है। 'X' का कार्य अर्थव्यवस्था के किस क्षेत्रक के अंतर्गत आएगा ?
questions.text_english: 'X' lives in a town. He cultivates flowers along with animal husbandry. The work of 'X' will fall under which sector of the economy?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Primary. The Primary sector includes all economic activities that involve direct extraction or use of natural resources. Both flower cultivation (agriculture) and animal husbandry involve working directly with nature. Therefore, the work of 'X' falls under the Primary sector. The Secondary sector involves manufacturing, the Tertiary sector involves services, and the Quaternary sector involves knowledge-based work.

questions.text:
दिए गए चित्र को देखिए और उसके नीचे दिए गए प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए :
चित्र में किया जाने वाला कार्य अर्थव्यवस्था के किस क्षेत्रक के अंतर्गत आता है ?
questions.text_english:
Look at the given picture and answer the question that follows:
The work being done in the picture falls under which sector of the economy?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Secondary. The picture shows workers engaged in garment manufacturing in a factory setting. The Secondary sector covers all activities that involve processing of raw materials and manufacturing of goods. Since the workers are transforming raw fabric into finished garments, this activity belongs to the Secondary (industrial/manufacturing) sector of the economy.

questions.text:
ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों में किसानों के लिए सरकारी बैंकों से ऋण लेना कठिन क्यों हो जाता है ? निम्नलिखित कारणों को पढ़िए और सबसे उपयुक्त विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
I. ऋणाधार का अभाव
II. जटिल प्रक्रिया
III. ऋण की उच्चतर लागत
IV. जागरूकता का अभाव
questions.text_english:
Why does it become difficult for farmers in rural areas to take loans from government banks? Read the following reasons and choose the most appropriate option:
I. Lack of collateral
II. Complicated procedure
III. Higher cost of borrowing
IV. Lack of awareness
questions.instruction_line: सबसे उपयुक्त विकल्प का चयन कीजिए

options.A: केवल I, II और III सही हैं।
options.B: केवल II, III और IV सही हैं।
options.C: केवल I, II और IV सही हैं।
options.D: केवल I, III और IV सही हैं।

options_english.A: Only I, II and III are correct.
options_english.B: Only II, III and IV are correct.
options_english.C: Only I, II and IV are correct.
options_english.D: Only I, III and IV are correct.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Only I, II and IV are correct. Farmers in rural areas find it difficult to get bank loans primarily because they lack collateral (assets to pledge as security), the banking procedures are complicated and bureaucratic, and they often lack awareness about formal credit facilities. The higher cost of borrowing (III) is actually more associated with informal money lenders rather than formal banks, which charge lower interest rates. Hence III is not a reason for avoiding formal banks.
questions.topic: Formal and informal sources of credit

questions.text: भारत के शहरी क्षेत्रों में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा समूह अपनी ऋण की आवश्यकताओं को पूरा करने के लिए अनौपचारिक स्रोतों पर निर्भर है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following groups in urban India depend on informal sources to meet their credit needs?

options.C: दोनों, गरीब और कम संपत्ति वाले परिवार
options.D: दोनों, समृद्ध और कम संपत्ति वाले परिवार

options_english.C: Both poor households and households with few assets
options_english.D: Both well-off households and households with few assets

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Both poor households and households with few assets. In urban India, both poor families and those with few assets find it difficult to access formal credit due to lack of collateral and documentation. As a result, they depend on informal sources such as moneylenders, friends, and relatives to meet their credit needs. Well-off households generally have easier access to formal banking credit.
questions.topic: Informal sources of credit in urban India

questions.text:
नीचे दो कथन I एवं II दिए गए हैं। दोनों कथनों को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़िए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
कथन I : प्रौद्योगिकी में तीव्र उन्नति वैश्वीकरण की प्रक्रिया को उत्प्रेरित करने वाला एक मुख्य कारक है।
कथन II : इसने लंबी दूरियों तक वस्तुओं की तीव्रतर आपूर्ति को कम लागत पर संभव किया है।
questions.text_english:
Two statements I and II are given below. Read both the statements carefully and choose the correct option:
Statement I: Rapid improvement in technology has been one major factor to stimulate the globalisation process.
Statement II: This has made much faster delivery of goods across long distances possible at lower costs.

options.A: कथन I और II दोनों सही हैं और कथन II, कथन I की सही व्याख्या है।
options.B: कथन I और II दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कथन II, कथन I की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
options.C: कथन I सही है, परन्तु कथन II गलत है।
options.D: कथन I गलत है, परन्तु कथन II सही है।

options_english.A: Both statements I and II are correct and statement II is the correct explanation of statement I.
options_english.B: Both statements I and II are correct, but statement II is not the correct explanation of statement I.
options_english.C: Statement I is correct, but statement II is incorrect.
options_english.D: Statement I is incorrect, but statement II is correct.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, and Statement II is the correct explanation of Statement I. Rapid technological improvement — especially in transport and communication such as containerisation, internet, and telecommunications — has directly enabled faster and cheaper delivery of goods over long distances, which is precisely how technology has stimulated the globalisation process. Statement II directly explains the mechanism by which Statement I operates.

(क) भारत में 'आधुनिक राष्ट्रवाद' के उदय में उपनिवेशवाद विरोधी आंदोलन की भूमिका को स्पष्ट कीजिए।

(ख) गाँधीजी ने क्यों कहा कि 'सत्याग्रह तो शुद्ध आत्मबल है' ? दो तर्क देकर स्पष्ट कीजिए।

sub_questions.text: भारत में 'आधुनिक राष्ट्रवाद' के उदय में उपनिवेशवाद विरोधी आंदोलन की भूमिका को स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the role of anti-colonial movement in the rise of 'modern nationalism' in India.

key_points: Anti-colonial movements united diverse people against a common enemy — British rule
Shared experience of exploitation and oppression created a collective national identity
Leaders like Gandhi channeled anti-colonial sentiment into organised mass movements

sub_questions.solution: The anti-colonial movement played a crucial role in the rise of modern nationalism in India. The shared experience of British exploitation and oppression brought together people from diverse regions, religions, and castes under a common cause. Movements like the Non-Cooperation Movement and Civil Disobedience Movement mobilised millions of Indians, fostering a sense of collective identity. Leaders like Mahatma Gandhi transformed anti-colonial resistance into organised mass participation, creating a unified national consciousness that transcended local differences.

sub_questions.text: गाँधीजी ने क्यों कहा कि 'सत्याग्रह तो शुद्ध आत्मबल है' ? दो तर्क देकर स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Why did Gandhiji say 'Satyagraha is pure soul-force'? Explain by giving two arguments.

key_points: Satyagraha relies on moral strength, not physical force or weapons
It seeks to change the oppressor's heart through truth and non-violence rather than coercion

sub_questions.solution: Gandhiji called Satyagraha pure soul-force because it relied entirely on moral and spiritual strength rather than physical force or weapons. First, a Satyagrahi confronts injustice through truth and non-violence, appealing to the conscience of the oppressor rather than using coercion. Second, it requires immense inner strength — the ability to endure suffering without retaliation — which Gandhiji believed was more powerful than any physical weapon in ultimately achieving justice.

questions.solution: This question has two options — (a) or (b). See sub_questions for complete model answers.

questions.text: संसाधनों के अंधाधुंध उपयोग के कारण उत्पन्न 'वैश्विक पारिस्थितिकी' की किन्हीं दो समस्याओं की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain any two problems of the 'global ecology' arising due to indiscriminate use of resources.

key_points: Global warming and climate change due to excessive burning of fossil fuels
Deforestation and loss of biodiversity due to overexploitation of forests and land

questions.solution: The indiscriminate use of resources has created serious problems for global ecology. First, the excessive burning of fossil fuels has led to a rise in greenhouse gases, causing global warming and climate change, which threatens weather patterns, sea levels, and ecosystems worldwide. Second, large-scale deforestation for agriculture and industry has led to destruction of habitats and loss of biodiversity, disrupting ecological balance and threatening the survival of numerous plant and animal species.
questions.topic: Global ecological problems due to resource overuse

questions.text: लैंगिक असमानता को दूर करने के कोई दो उपाय सुझाइए।
questions.text_english: Suggest any two measures to remove gender inequality.

key_points: Ensure equal access to education for girls at all levels
Enact and enforce laws that provide equal political representation and workplace rights for women

questions.solution: Two important measures to remove gender inequality are: First, ensuring equal access to education for girls at all levels, including higher and professional education, which empowers women economically and socially and enables them to participate fully in public life. Second, enacting and strictly enforcing laws that guarantee equal political representation for women, such as reservation of seats in legislatures, along with laws against gender-based discrimination in workplaces and equal pay for equal work.
questions.topic: Gender inequality and measures to address it

questions.text: भारत में 1990 के दशक में शुरू की गई उदारीकरण की प्रक्रिया ने किस प्रकार वैश्वीकरण को बढ़ावा दिया ? स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: How did the process of liberalisation initiated in India in the 1990s, promote globalisation? Explain.

key_points: Liberalisation removed trade barriers, allowing free flow of goods and capital
Opening of Indian markets to foreign investment attracted multinational companies

questions.solution: The liberalisation process initiated in India in the 1990s significantly promoted globalisation by dismantling trade barriers such as import tariffs, quotas, and licensing requirements. This allowed the free flow of goods, services, and capital across borders. The opening of Indian markets to foreign direct investment attracted multinational companies, integrating India into the global economy. Reduced government controls also allowed Indian companies to expand internationally, increasing India's participation in global trade and investment networks.

questions.text: "आदिवासी किसानों ने महात्मा गाँधी के संदेश और 'स्वराज' के विचार का कुछ और ही मतलब निकाला।" असहयोग आंदोलन के संदर्भ में इस कथन की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: "Tribal peasants interpreted the message of Mahatma Gandhi and the idea of 'Swaraj' in yet another way." Explain the statement in the context of Non-Cooperation Movement.

key_points: Tribal peasants connected Swaraj to their specific grievances — forest laws and loss of access to forests
In Gudem Hills, Alluri Sitaram Raju led tribal rebellions believing Swaraj meant freedom from colonial forest laws
Tribals participated in Non-Cooperation but their interpretation was distinct from mainstream nationalist agenda

questions.solution: Tribal peasants gave the concept of Swaraj a meaning rooted in their own specific grievances against colonial rule. In the Gudem Hills of Andhra Pradesh, the colonial government's forest laws prevented tribals from entering forests to graze cattle, collect wood, and pursue traditional practices, causing immense hardship. Under the leadership of Alluri Sitaram Raju, tribals participated in the Non-Cooperation Movement but interpreted Swaraj as freedom from these restrictive forest laws and the restoration of their traditional rights over forests and lands. Unlike urban nationalists who sought political independence, tribal peasants fought for their immediate economic survival and customary forest rights. This shows how different sections of Indian society joined the national movement but with their own distinct aspirations and interpretations of freedom.

questions.text:
रिंझा की कहानी को पढ़िए और उसके नीचे दिए गए प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए :

रिंझा की कहानी

रिंझा असम में डिफु के बाहरी क्षेत्र में अपने परिवार के साथ एक छोटे गाँव में रहती है। वह अपने परिवार के सदस्यों द्वारा एक भूमि के टुकड़े पर उगी वनस्पति को काटकर व जलाकर साफ करते देख कर आनन्द का अनुभव करती है। वह प्राय: परिवार के सदस्यों के साथ बाँस के नाले द्वारा समीप के झरने से पानी लाकर अपने खेत को सिंचित करने में सहायता करती है। वह अपने परिस्थान से लगाव रखती है और जब तक संभव हो यहाँ रहना चाहती है। परन्तु इस छोटी बच्ची को अपने खेत में मिट्टी की घटती उर्वरता के बारे में कुछ भी पता नहीं है जिसके कारण उसके परिवार को अगले वर्ष नए भूमि के टुकड़े की तलाश करनी होगी।

रिंझा का परिवार किस प्रकार की खेती कर रहा है ? उसकी किन्हीं दो विशेषताओं का वर्णन कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
Read the story of Rinjha and answer the question that follows:

Story of Rinjha

Rinjha lived with her family in a small village at the outskirts of Diphu in Assam. She enjoys watching her family members clearing, slashing and burning a patch of land for cultivation. She often helps them in irrigating the fields with water running through a bamboo canal from the nearby spring. She loves the surroundings and wants to stay here as long as she can, but this little girl has no idea about the declining fertility of the soil and her family's search for a fresh patch of land in the next season.

What type of farming is Rinjha's family doing? Describe any two of its characteristics.
questions.instruction_line: रिंझा की कहानी को पढ़िए और उत्तर दीजिए
questions.instruction_line_english: Read the story of Rinjha and answer

key_points: Rinjha's family practices Shifting Cultivation (Jhum cultivation)
Land is cleared by slashing and burning vegetation
The family moves to a new patch of land when soil fertility declines

questions.solution: Rinjha's family is practising Shifting Cultivation, also known as Jhum cultivation or slash-and-burn agriculture. It is practised by tribal communities in the northeastern states of India. Two of its characteristics are: First, farmers clear a patch of forest by cutting and burning the vegetation, which releases nutrients into the soil and makes it temporarily fertile for cultivation. Second, once the soil's fertility declines after a few years of cultivation, the family abandons that patch and moves to a new piece of forest land, repeating the process. This makes it a nomadic form of agriculture with no permanent settlement.

questions.text: "वह लोकतांत्रिक शासन व्यवस्था अच्छी मानी जाती है जिसमें अधिक-से-अधिक नागरिकों को राजनीतिक सत्ता में हिस्सेदार बनाया जाए।" उपयुक्त तर्कों सहित इस कथन की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: "That democratic system of government is considered good in which maximum number of citizens are made stakeholders in political power." Explain the statement with suitable arguments.

key_points: Wider participation ensures that diverse voices are heard and public policies reflect the needs of all sections
Political inclusion reduces social conflict and strengthens social cohesion
Citizens who participate in governance develop a sense of ownership and responsibility

questions.solution: A democratic government is considered good when it maximises citizen participation in political power for several reasons. First, when more citizens participate, government policies better reflect the needs and aspirations of diverse sections of society, leading to more equitable and just governance. Second, broader political inclusion reduces social tensions and conflicts because marginalised groups feel represented and heard within the system. Third, citizens who are stakeholders in political power develop a sense of civic responsibility and ownership of governance, leading to more stable and accountable institutions. Thus, genuine democracy means not just periodic elections but continuous and meaningful participation of all citizens in decision-making.
questions.topic: Democratic participation and outcomes of democracy

sub_questions.text_english: Explain the importance of political parties in democracy.

key_points: Political parties contest elections and enable citizens to choose their government
They aggregate and articulate public opinion, forming policies and governing the country
Opposition parties keep the ruling party accountable and provide alternative policies

sub_questions.solution: Political parties are essential in a democracy. First, they contest elections, allowing citizens to choose their representatives and thereby form the government. Second, they aggregate public opinions and interests, formulate policies, and implement them when in power, thus translating popular will into governance. Third, opposition parties play a vital role by criticising government decisions, keeping the ruling party accountable, and offering alternative policies, which ensures democratic checks and balances. Without political parties, modern democracy would be impossible as they connect citizens to the government and ensure peaceful transfer of power.

sub_questions.text: भारत ने बहुदलीय व्यवस्था को क्यों अपनाया ? उचित तर्कों सहित व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Why did India adopt the multiparty system? Explain with suitable arguments.

key_points: India's vast social diversity in terms of region, language, religion, and caste required multiple parties to represent varied interests
A multiparty system allows various groups to participate in politics and prevents domination by a single party
It ensures that a wider range of citizen interests are reflected in governance and policy

sub_questions.solution: India adopted the multiparty system because of its immense social, cultural, linguistic, and regional diversity. A single or two-party system would be inadequate to represent the vast variety of communities, castes, religions, and regional interests that exist across the country. The multiparty system allows different sections of society — including minorities, regional communities, and ideological groups — to participate meaningfully in the political process. It prevents any single group from dominating governance and ensures that policies reflect the aspirations of all sections, making the democracy more inclusive, representative, and responsive to the needs of a diverse population.

questions.solution: This question has two options — (a) or (b). See sub_questions for complete model answers.

questions.text: भारतीय अर्थव्यवस्था के सार्वजनिक एवं निजी क्षेत्र में अंतर को उदाहरण सहित स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain the difference between public and private sector of Indian economy with example.

key_points: In the public sector, assets and services are owned and managed by the government; example — Indian Railways, BHEL
In the private sector, assets and enterprises are owned and managed by private individuals or companies; example — Tata Motors, Reliance Industries
Public sector aims at social welfare and may run at a loss, while private sector is profit-driven

questions.solution: In the public sector, the government owns and manages most of the assets and provides services. The primary aim is not profit but public welfare and service to citizens. Examples include Indian Railways, ONGC, and BHEL. In the private sector, enterprises are owned and managed by private individuals or companies, and the primary motive is profit. Examples include Tata Motors, Infosys, and Reliance Industries. The key difference is that while the public sector uses taxpayers' money for social objectives such as healthcare, education, and infrastructure, the private sector operates competitively to maximise profits for its owners and shareholders.
questions.topic: Public and private sector in India

OR

sub_questions.text: प्रशासनिक व्यवस्था को तर्कसंगत और कुशल बनाने में 'नेपोलियन संहिता' के महत्त्व का विश्लेषण कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Analyse the significance of the 'Napoleonic Code' in making the administrative system rational and efficient.

key_points: It abolished feudal privileges and established equality before law
It guaranteed the right to property and secured contractual obligations
It standardised the legal and administrative system across French territories
It promoted meritocracy by removing birth-based privileges
It influenced the legal systems of other European countries beyond France

sub_questions.solution: The Napoleonic Code, introduced in 1804, was a landmark in making the administrative and legal system rational and efficient. First, it abolished all privileges based on birth and established equality before the law, replacing the arbitrary feudal system with a uniform legal code applicable to all citizens. Second, it guaranteed the right to property and secured contractual obligations, providing a stable environment for economic activity and trade. Third, by standardising laws across French territories, it eliminated confusion arising from multiple local customs and regulations, making governance more efficient. Fourth, it promoted merit over birth in appointments to public offices, creating a more capable administration. Finally, the Code influenced legal reforms across Europe, contributing to modernisation beyond France.

sub_questions.text: उन्नीसवीं सदी के शुरुआती दशकों में यूरोप में उदारवाद किस प्रकार राष्ट्रीय एकता से जुड़ा हुआ था ? विश्लेषण कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: How was liberalism allied to national unity in Europe in the early decades of the 19th century? Analyse.

key_points: Liberalism demanded individual freedom, rule of law, and representative government
Middle class liberals sought a unified nation-state to replace fragmented feudal kingdoms
Freedom of press and political association helped spread nationalist ideas
The 1848 revolutions showed the alliance of liberal and nationalist demands across Europe
Free trade within a unified territory was seen as economically beneficial

sub_questions.solution: In the early decades of the 19th century, liberalism and nationalism were closely intertwined in Europe. Liberals, who were mainly from the educated middle class, advocated individual freedoms, equality before law, and representative government. They recognised that achieving these goals required the creation of unified nation-states in place of the fragmented, autocratic kingdoms. For example, German merchants and professionals sought a unified Germany that would allow free movement of goods and people, eliminate trade barriers, and create a common currency and legal system. The 1848 revolutions across Europe demonstrated this alliance, as liberals simultaneously demanded constitutional governments and national unification. Freedom of the press further helped spread nationalist ideas. Thus, liberal and nationalist goals mutually reinforced each other.

OR

sub_questions.text: "विनिर्माण उद्योग किसी देश के आर्थिक विकास की रीढ़ समझे जाते हैं।" इस कथन को न्यायसंगत ठहराइए।
sub_questions.text_english: "Manufacturing industries are considered the backbone of the economic development of a country." Justify the statement.

key_points: Manufacturing generates large-scale employment for the growing workforce
It transforms raw materials into value-added goods, increasing national income
It earns foreign exchange through exports, strengthening the economy
Industrial development creates ancillary industries and promotes urbanisation
Modern industries provide technology and machinery used in other sectors like agriculture

sub_questions.solution: Manufacturing industries are rightly considered the backbone of economic development for several reasons. First, they generate large-scale employment for millions of workers, particularly in developing countries with growing populations, reducing unemployment and raising living standards. Second, manufacturing transforms raw materials into value-added finished goods, significantly increasing national income and GDP. Third, manufactured goods are major export items that earn valuable foreign exchange, strengthening the country's balance of payments. Fourth, industrial growth promotes urbanisation and stimulates the growth of ancillary industries, service sectors, and infrastructure. Fifth, advanced manufacturing produces machinery, fertilisers, and equipment that modernise agriculture and other sectors, fostering overall economic progress across the nation.

sub_questions.text: "कृषि तथा उद्योग एक-दूसरे के पूरक हैं।" इस कथन को न्यायसंगत ठहराइए।
sub_questions.text_english: "Agriculture and industries complement each other." Justify the statement.

key_points: Agriculture provides raw materials (cotton, jute, sugarcane) to agro-based industries
Industries manufacture fertilisers, pesticides, and farm machinery used in agriculture
Agricultural surplus generates income for rural people who become consumers of industrial products
Industries process agricultural produce, adding value and reducing post-harvest losses
Both sectors together drive the overall economic growth of the country

sub_questions.solution: Agriculture and industries complement each other in multiple ways. Agriculture supplies raw materials such as cotton, jute, sugarcane, and oilseeds to agro-based industries like textiles, sugar mills, and edible oil factories, enabling industrial production. Conversely, industries manufacture fertilisers, pesticides, irrigation equipment, and farm machinery that increase agricultural productivity. Agricultural income raises the purchasing power of rural populations, who then become consumers of industrial goods, stimulating industrial demand. Industries process and add value to agricultural produce, reducing post-harvest losses and improving farmer incomes. Thus, growth in one sector stimulates growth in the other, making agriculture and industry interdependent and mutually complementary pillars of economic development.

questions.text_english:
(a) Explain any five bases for assessing the outcomes of democracy.
OR
(b) Explain any five values of democracy.

sub_questions.text: लोकतंत्र के परिणामों का मूल्यांकन करने वाले किन्हीं पाँच आधारों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain any five bases for assessing the outcomes of democracy.

key_points: Accountable and responsive government — citizens can hold representatives accountable
Legitimate government — decisions taken through proper procedures and majority consent
Economic growth and development — ensuring equitable distribution of resources
Reduction in social inequalities — addressing disparities of caste, gender, and class
Protection of individual rights and dignity — freedom, justice, and civil liberties

sub_questions.solution: The outcomes of democracy can be assessed on five important bases. First, a good democracy must produce an accountable government where elected representatives are answerable to citizens and can be voted out if they fail to perform. Second, it should produce a legitimate government, one whose decisions are taken through proper procedures and accepted by the people. Third, democracy should promote economic growth and ensure equitable distribution of wealth and resources among all sections. Fourth, it must reduce social inequalities based on caste, gender, class, and religion, ensuring every citizen has dignity and equal opportunities. Fifth, democracy must protect individual rights and civil liberties, guaranteeing freedom of speech, religion, and justice for all.

sub_questions.text: लोकतंत्र के किन्हीं पाँच मूल्यों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain any five values of democracy.

key_points: Equality — all citizens are equal before the law regardless of birth or status
Liberty — freedom of thought, expression, and participation in governance
Fraternity — a sense of brotherhood and solidarity among citizens
Justice — social, economic, and political justice for all sections
Dignity — respect for every individual's inherent human dignity

sub_questions.solution: Democracy is founded on several core values. First, equality ensures that every citizen is equal before the law and has an equal vote, regardless of wealth, caste, or religion. Second, liberty guarantees individuals freedom of speech, expression, and participation in the political process without fear. Third, fraternity promotes a sense of brotherhood and solidarity among diverse communities, fostering national unity. Fourth, justice — social, economic, and political — ensures that all citizens have access to fair treatment and opportunities, reducing discrimination. Fifth, human dignity upholds the inherent worth of every person and ensures that governance respects individual rights and does not treat any citizen as inferior. Together, these values make democracy the most humane and fair form of governance.

questions.solution: This question has two options — (a) or (b). See sub_questions for complete model answers.

questions.text:
(क) "हाल के प्रमाण बताते हैं कि देश के कई भागों में भूमिगत जल का अति उपयोग एक गंभीर संकट बनता जा रहा है।" विकास की धारणीयता के संदर्भ में इस कथन का मूल्यांकन कीजिए।

questions.text_english:
(a) "Recent evidence suggests that overuse of groundwater is becoming a serious threat in many parts of the country." Evaluate the statement in the context of sustainability of development.
OR

sub_questions.text: "हाल के प्रमाण बताते हैं कि देश के कई भागों में भूमिगत जल का अति उपयोग एक गंभीर संकट बनता जा रहा है।" विकास की धारणीयता के संदर्भ में इस कथन का मूल्यांकन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: "Recent evidence suggests that overuse of groundwater is becoming a serious threat in many parts of the country." Evaluate the statement in the context of sustainability of development.

key_points: Overuse of groundwater depletes a non-renewable resource, threatening future availability
Falling water tables affect agriculture, drinking water, and rural livelihoods
Sustainable development requires meeting present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet theirs
Excessive extraction for irrigation (Green Revolution) and industrial use are key causes
Measures like rainwater harvesting, drip irrigation, and legal regulations are needed

sub_questions.solution: The overuse of groundwater is a direct threat to the sustainability of development. Sustainable development means meeting the present generation's needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet theirs. Groundwater is a finite resource, and its excessive extraction — largely for agricultural irrigation, especially in Green Revolution states like Punjab and Haryana — has caused water tables to fall alarmingly. This endangers agricultural production, drinking water supply, and rural livelihoods for future generations. Industries also draw heavily on groundwater, worsening the crisis. Unless corrective measures like rainwater harvesting, drip irrigation, groundwater regulation laws, and crop diversification are adopted urgently, this unsustainable extraction will undermine long-term economic and ecological development for the entire nation.

sub_questions.text: "विभिन्न श्रेणी के लोगों के विकास के लक्ष्य भिन्न हो सकते हैं।" इस कथन का मूल्यांकन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: "The development goals of different categories of people may differ." Evaluate the statement.

key_points: Development goals differ because people have different needs, aspirations, and circumstances
A landless labourer seeks employment and fair wages; an industrialist seeks profits
A woman may prioritise safety and education; a farmer may prioritise irrigation facilities
National development must balance conflicting goals through fair policies
No single indicator can capture all development goals; multiple indicators are needed

sub_questions.solution: The statement that development goals differ among different categories of people is entirely valid. Development is not a one-size-fits-all concept — it encompasses the varied aspirations and needs of different groups. A landless agricultural labourer's primary goal may be steady employment and fair wages, while an industrialist seeks profits and market expansion. A woman living in a village may prioritise personal safety, access to education, and health facilities. A farmer may primarily want better irrigation and assured prices for crops. These goals may sometimes conflict — a dam project may benefit industrial and urban users while displacing tribal communities. Therefore, national development policies must balance these differing goals through inclusive planning, ensuring that the progress of one group does not come at the cost of another's well-being.

दिए गए स्रोत को पढ़िए और उसके नीचे दिए गए प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए :

प्रिंट और प्रतिबंध

मुद्रित शब्द की ताकत का अंदाज़ा अकसर सरकार द्वारा उसको नियंत्रित करने की कोशिशों से मिलता है। भारत में औपनिवेशिक प्रशासन हमेशा तमाम किताबों और पत्र-पत्रिकाओं पर नज़र रखता था तथा प्रेस पर नियंत्रण रखने के लिए बहुत-से कानून पारित करता था।

पहले विश्व युद्ध के दौरान, भारतीय रक्षा नियम के तहत, 22 अखबारों को जमानत देनी पड़ी थी। इनमें से 18 ने सरकारी आदेश मानने की जगह खुद को बंद कर देना उचित समझा। रॉलट के अधीन कार्यरत षड्यंत्र समिति ने 1919 में विभिन्न अखबारों के खिलाफ जुर्माना आदि कार्रवाइयों को और सख्त बना दिया। द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध की शुरुआत पर, भारतीय रक्षा अधिनियम पारित किया गया, ताकि युद्ध-संबंधी विषयों को सेंसर किया जा सके। भारत छोड़ो आंदोलन से जुड़ी तमाम रपटें इसी के तहत सेंसर होती थीं। अगस्त 1942 में तकरीबन 90 अखबारों का दमन किया गया।
questions.text_english:
Read the given source and answer the questions that follow:

Print and Censorship

The power of the printed word is most often seen in the way governments seek to regulate and suppress print. The colonial government kept continuous track of all books and newspapers published in India and passed numerous laws to control the press.

During the First World War, under the Defence of India Rules, 22 newspapers had to furnish securities. Of these, 18 shut down rather than comply with government orders. The Sedition Committee Report under Rowlatt in 1919 further strengthened controls that led to imposition of penalties on various newspapers. At the outbreak of the Second World War, the Defence of India Act was passed, allowing censoring of reports of war-related topics. All reports about the Quit India movement came under its purview. In August 1942, about 90 newspapers were suppressed.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain the meaning of 'censor'.

key_points: Censor means the official suppression or examination of written, printed, or broadcast material to remove parts considered politically sensitive or harmful

sub_questions.solution: To censor means to examine books, newspapers, films, or other media and suppress or remove content that the government considers politically sensitive, dangerous, or harmful to its authority. In the colonial context, it meant that the British government reviewed and blocked any printed material that criticized colonial rule or reported on nationalist movements.

sub_questions.text: औपनिवेशिक प्रशासन किताबों और पत्र-पत्रिकाओं पर क्यों नज़र रखता था ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why did the colonial administration keep an eye on books and newspapers?

key_points: The colonial government feared that printed material could spread nationalist ideas, criticism of British rule, and inspire Indians to revolt

sub_questions.solution: The colonial administration kept a close watch on books and newspapers because it feared the power of the printed word to spread nationalist ideas, criticize British rule, and inspire people to resist colonial authority. Printed material could rapidly mobilise public opinion against the government across a large population, threatening British control over India. To prevent this, numerous laws were enacted to regulate and suppress the press.

sub_questions.text: गाँधीजी ने रॉलट एक्ट के विरुद्ध देशव्यापी सत्याग्रह क्यों शुरू किया ? किन्हीं दो कारणों को स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Why did Gandhiji start a nationwide Satyagraha against the Rowlatt Act? Explain any two reasons.

key_points: The Rowlatt Act allowed the government to arrest and detain Indians without trial, violating basic civil liberties
It suppressed political activity and freedom of expression, angering nationalists and the general public

sub_questions.solution: Gandhiji launched a nationwide Satyagraha against the Rowlatt Act for two main reasons. First, the Act empowered the British government to imprison any Indian without trial and detain political prisoners indefinitely, which was a severe violation of the fundamental civil liberties of Indians and went against all principles of justice. Second, the Act was specifically designed to crush political dissent and suppress the growing nationalist movement by giving the colonial government sweeping powers to silence critics and activists, which deeply angered Indians who had expected political reforms after their service during World War I.

दिए गए स्रोत को पढ़िए और उसके नीचे दिए गए प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए :

ब्राज़ील का एक प्रयोग

ब्राज़ील के शहर पोर्टो एलेग्रे ने विकेंद्रीकरण और नागरिकों की सक्रिय भागीदारी वाले लोकतंत्र के मेल का एक विलक्षण प्रयोग किया है। इस शहर के नगर-परिषद के समानांतर एक संगठन खड़ा किया गया और अपने शहर के बारे में वास्तविक फैसले करने का अधिकार स्थानीय निवासियों को दिया गया है। इस शहर के करीब 13 लाख लोग अपने शहर का बजट तैयार करने में भागीदारी करते हैं। शहर को अनेक उप-क्षेत्रों में बाँटा गया है — लगभग वैसे ही जिन्हें हम वार्ड कहते हैं। हर उप-क्षेत्र की अपनी-अपनी बैठक होती है जिसका स्वरूप ग्राम सभा की तरह है और इसमें उस इलाके के सभी नागरिक भाग ले सकते हैं। फिर, कुछ बैठकें पूरे शहर को प्रभावित करने वाले मुद्दों पर होती हैं और उसमें शहर का कोई भी नागरिक भाग ले सकता है। इसमें शहर के बजट पर चर्चा होती है। इसके बाद इन प्रस्तावों को नगरपालिका के सामने पेश किया जाता है जो अंतिम फैसला लेती है।
questions.text_english:
Read the given source and answer the questions that follow:

An Experiment in Brazil

A city called Porto Alegre in Brazil has carried out an extraordinary experiment in combining decentralisation with participative democracy. The city has set up a parallel organisation operating alongside the municipal council, enabling local inhabitants to take real decisions for their city. The nearly 13 lakh people in this city get to participate in making the budget for their own city. The city is divided into many sectors or what we call wards. Each sector has a meeting, like that of the gram sabha, in which anyone living in that area can participate. There are some meetings to discuss issues that affect the entire city. Any citizen of the city can participate in those meetings. The budget of the city is discussed in these meetings. The proposals are put to the municipality that takes a final decision about it.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain the meaning of 'participatory democracy'.

key_points: Participatory democracy means a system where citizens directly and actively participate in political decision-making beyond merely voting in elections

sub_questions.solution: Participatory democracy refers to a form of democratic governance in which citizens actively and directly take part in political decision-making processes — such as budget planning, local governance, and policy formulation — beyond merely voting in periodic elections. It empowers ordinary people to have a real say in matters that affect their daily lives.

sub_questions.text: शक्तियों के बँटवारे के संदर्भ में, दिया गया उदाहरण किस प्रकार की शासन प्रणाली को परिभाषित करता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: In the context of separation of powers, the given example defines which type of government?

key_points: The example defines a Federal type of government, with power shared between the central/municipal authority and local ward-level bodies

sub_questions.solution: The example of Porto Alegre defines a Federal type of government in the context of separation of powers. Power is shared between the municipal council (central city authority) and local sector-level or ward-level bodies where citizens directly participate. This decentralisation of power from a central authority to smaller local units is the defining feature of a federal arrangement.

sub_questions.text: ब्राज़ील के उपर्युक्त उदाहरण से लगभग मिलती-जुलती भारत की व्यवस्था के गठन का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Describe the structure of the system in India which is almost similar to the above example of Brazil.

key_points: India's Panchayati Raj system at the village level is similar to Brazil's experiment
Gram Sabha — all voters of the village participate in decision-making at the local level
Panchayats handle local governance, development plans, and budget at the village level

sub_questions.solution: India's Panchayati Raj system closely resembles the Porto Alegre experiment in Brazil. At the village level, the Gram Sabha — comprising all registered voters of the village — meets periodically to discuss and decide on local development plans, budgets, and public welfare programmes. Above the Gram Sabha is the Gram Panchayat, the elected village council that implements decisions. This three-tier structure of village, block, and district panchayats ensures decentralisation of power, enabling ordinary citizens to directly participate in local governance and decisions that affect their everyday lives.

सहकारी समितियों से ऋण

बैंकों के अलावा ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों में सस्ते ऋण का एक अन्य प्रमुख स्रोत सहकारी समितियाँ हैं। सहकारी समिति के सदस्य अपने संसाधनों को कुछ क्षेत्रों में सहयोग के लिए एकत्र करते हैं। कई प्रकार की सहकारी समितियाँ संभव हैं, जैसे — किसानों, बुनकरों एवं औद्योगिक मज़दूरों इत्यादि की सहकारी समितियाँ। कृषक सहकारी समिति सोनपुर के नज़दीक एक गाँव में काम करती है। इसके 2300 किसान सदस्य हैं। यह अपने सदस्यों से जमा प्राप्त करती है। इस जमा पूँजी को ऋणाधार मानते हुए, इस सहकारी समिति ने बैंक से बड़ा ऋण प्राप्त किया है। इस पूँजी का इस्तेमाल सदस्यों को कर्ज़ देने के लिए किया जाता है। यह ऋण लौटाने के बाद कर्ज़ का दूसरा दौर शुरू किया जा सकता है।

कृषक सहकारी समिति कृषि उपकरण खरीदने, खेती तथा कृषि व्यापार करने, मछली पकड़ने, घर बनाने और अन्य विभिन्न प्रकार के खर्चों के लिए ऋण मुहैया कराती है।
questions.text_english:
Read the given source and answer the questions that follow:

Loans From Cooperatives

Besides banks, the other major source of cheap credit in rural areas are the cooperative societies (or cooperatives). Members of a cooperative pool their resources for cooperation in certain areas. There are several types of cooperatives possible such as farmers cooperatives, weavers cooperatives, industrial workers cooperatives, etc. Krishak Cooperative functions in a village not very far away from Sonpur. It has 2300 farmers as members. It accepts deposits from its members. With these deposits as collateral, the Cooperative has obtained a large loan from the bank. These funds are used to provide loans to members. Once these loans are repaid, another round of lending can take place.

Krishak Cooperative provides loans for the purchase of agricultural implements, loans for cultivation and agricultural trade, fishery loans, loans for construction of houses and for a variety of other expenses.

sub_questions.text_english: Cooperative societies come under which source of credit?

key_points: Cooperative societies come under the Formal (institutional) source of credit

sub_questions.solution: Cooperative societies come under the Formal (institutional) source of credit. They are registered organisations that function under government regulations and provide credit at relatively lower interest rates to their members, unlike informal sources such as moneylenders.

sub_questions.text: सहकारी समितियों की पूँजी के किन्हीं दो स्रोतों का उल्लेख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Mention any two sources of capital of cooperative societies.

key_points: Deposits collected from members
Loans obtained from commercial banks using members' deposits as collateral

sub_questions.solution: The two main sources of capital of cooperative societies are: first, deposits collected from member farmers, which form the base capital of the cooperative; and second, loans obtained from commercial banks by using these member deposits as collateral, which significantly increases the funds available for lending to members.

sub_questions.text: किसानों की आय वृद्धि में सहकारी समितियों की भूमिका को स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the role of cooperative societies in increasing the income of farmers.

key_points: Provide cheap credit for purchasing agricultural implements, seeds, and fertilisers, reducing production costs
Enable farmers to invest in better farming practices, increasing agricultural output and income

sub_questions.solution: Cooperative societies play an important role in increasing farmers' income in two key ways. First, they provide loans at much lower interest rates than informal moneylenders for purchasing agricultural implements, seeds, fertilisers, and other inputs, which reduces the cost of cultivation and allows farmers to invest in productivity-enhancing practices. Second, by providing credit for agricultural trade, fishery, and house construction, cooperatives help farmers diversify their economic activities, reducing dependence on a single source of income and thereby increasing their overall earnings and financial security.
